title: Fish Fingers
description: Fish Fingers are a classic Continental appetizer made with firm white fish coated in a crispy panko breadcrumb crust and fried until golden brown. Served with tartar sauce or lemon-dill aioli, they are crunchy on the outside and tender inside.

ingredients.title: For the Fish Fingers
items: Firm white fish fillets (cod, haddock, halibut, or seabass), skinless and boneless – 500 g
All-purpose flour (seasoned lightly with salt & pepper) – 2 tbsp
Eggs, beaten with 1 tbsp cold water – 2

ingredients.title: For the Accompaniment
items: Homemade tartar sauce or lemon-dill aioli – 150 g
Microgreens or lightly dressed mesclun salad

ingredients.title: For Frying
items: Neutral oil with a high smoke point (sunflower, grapeseed, or peanut oil)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Fish
steps: Cut fish fillets into even batons (approx. 2 cm × 8 cm).
Pat dry thoroughly with kitchen towel.
Season with salt, pepper, lemon zest, and parsley.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Coating
steps: Mix panko breadcrumbs, Parmesan, and smoked paprika.
Set up a dredging station with flour, egg wash, and breadcrumb mixture.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Coat the Fish
steps: Dredge each fish baton in flour and shake off the excess.
Dip into the egg wash, then coat generously in the panko mixture.
Press lightly so the crumbs adhere.
Lay on parchment and refrigerate for 20 minutes to help the crust set.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Frying
steps: Heat oil in a deep pan to 180°C (350°F).
Fry fish fingers in small batches for 2–3 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
Remove and drain on a wire rack.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Serving
steps: Plate with a quenelle of tartar sauce or lemon-dill aioli.
Serve with lemon wedges and microgreens.
Optional: Dust the plate rim with smoked paprika or serve atop a pea purée.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot with tartar sauce or lemon-dill aioli.
Pair with French fries, coleslaw, or a fresh green salad.
Garnish with lemon wedges and microgreens for an elegant presentation.

chefTips: Panko breadcrumbs create a light, crispy coating, while Parmesan adds extra umami flavor.
Refrigerate the coated fish for 20 minutes before frying to help the coating stay intact.
Drain on a wire rack instead of paper towels to maintain crispness.
For a lighter version, bake at 200°C (400°F) with a drizzle of olive oil, turning once for even browning.
